conceptPrimer.heading: First Law & the Physics Sign Convention
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: $\Delta Q = \Delta U + \Delta W$ with $\Delta W$ = work done BY the gas ($\int P\,dV$, area under the $P$-$V$ curve; clockwise cycle $\Rightarrow \Delta W > 0$, $\Delta U_{\text{cycle}} = 0$). Chemistry flips it ($\Delta U = q + w_{\text{on}}$) — read which work is asked! Micro-check: expansion absorbing $100\,\text{J}$ while doing $40\,\text{J}$: $\Delta U = 60\,\text{J}$.

conceptPrimer.heading: Degrees of Freedom, Mayer's Relation & Gamma
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: $U = \frac{f}{2}nRT$ (monatomic $f = 3$, rigid diatomic $f = 5$); $C_P - C_V = R$ and $\gamma = \frac{C_P}{C_V} = 1 + \frac{2}{f}$: monatomic $5/3 \approx 1.67$, diatomic $7/5 = 1.4$. Micro-check: diatomic $C_V = \frac{5}{2}R$, $C_P = \frac{7}{2}R$.

conceptPrimer.heading: The Four Processes at a Glance
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Isochoric: $W = 0$, $\Delta Q = \Delta U$. Isobaric: $W = P\Delta V = nR\Delta T$. Isothermal: $\Delta U = 0$, $\Delta Q = W = nRT\ln\frac{V_2}{V_1}$, bulk modulus $K_T = P$. Adiabatic: $\Delta Q = 0$, $W = -\Delta U$, $PV^\gamma = \text{const}$, $TV^{\gamma-1} = \text{const}$, slope $\gamma\times$ steeper than isotherm. Micro-check: isothermal doubling of $V$: $W = nRT\ln 2$.

conceptPrimer.heading: Free Expansion: the Irreversible Exception
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Expansion into vacuum: $P_{\text{ext}} = 0 \Rightarrow W = 0$; no heat exchange $\Rightarrow \Delta Q = 0$; so $\Delta U = 0$ and an IDEAL gas suffers NO temperature change — even though $PV^\gamma = \text{const}$ does NOT apply (it holds only for reversible adiabats). Micro-check: an irreversible adiabat is not a $PV^\gamma$ curve.

conceptPrimer.heading: Carnot Engine & Refrigerator COP
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Reversible Carnot between $T_H$ and $T_C$ (KELVIN): $\eta = 1 - \frac{T_C}{T_H} = \frac{W}{Q_H}$; refrigerator COP $= \frac{Q_C}{W} = \frac{T_C}{T_H - T_C}$. Lowering $T_C$ by $\Delta T$ helps $\eta$ MORE than raising $T_H$ by the same $\Delta T$. Micro-check: $T_H = 500$, $T_C = 300$: $\eta = 0.4$; drop $T_C$ to $290$: $\eta = 0.42$ vs raising $T_H$ to $510$: $\eta \approx 0.412$.

conceptPrimer.heading: Second Law in Two Voices
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Kelvin-Planck: no cyclic engine converts heat to work with $100\%$ efficiency. Clausius: heat never flows spontaneously cold $\to$ hot without external work. Both forbid perpetual motions of the second kind. Micro-check: a perfect engine ($\eta = 1$) would violate Kelvin-Planck outright.

memoryHooks: Isochoric: no work. Isobaric: $P\Delta V$. Isothermal: $nRT\ln$. Adiabatic: $-\Delta U$.
$PV^\gamma$: reversible only; free expansion is the exception.
Sink cooling beats source heating for efficiency.
Cycle: $\Delta U = 0$; net work = enclosed area.
commonMistakes: Mixing physics and chemistry sign conventions.
Applying $PV^\gamma$ to free or irreversible expansion.
Claiming any real engine beats the Carnot limit.
Counting vibrational degrees for rigid-diatomic questions.
Saying $\Delta U \ne 0$ for isothermal ideal-gas processes.
Dropping the kelvin requirement in COP sums.
